data: A built-in MCP server lets Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf search your library and copy assets into your project. Also: assethoard:// links, searchable audio metadata, EXR and HDR support, and batch image export.

AssetHoard is a local-first asset manager for game developers and digital artists. This release adds an MCP server, assethoard:// links, searchable and editable audio metadata, EXR and HDR support, and batch image export.

🤖 MCP server

AssetHoard now has a built-in MCP server. Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf can use it to search your library and copy assets into your project. Setup steps are in the MCP docs.

  • Setup. Turn it on in Settings > MCP Server. It's off by default, only listens on your machine and needs a token. The settings page gives you a setup command to paste into your client. Claude Desktop connects through mcp-remote for now.
  • Search. Same as the search bar: by name with typo tolerance, and by meaning if semantic search is on. Results can be filtered by file type, tag, category or bundle. Clients can also view thumbnails, asset details and bundle contents (50 assets per page).
  • Export. Copy assets or bundles to a folder along with their dependencies, such as Godot resources, Unreal references and model textures. Existing files are never overwritten.
  • Write tools. Off unless you enable Allow write tools. Clients can then manage bundles, tags, categories and projects. Nothing can be deleted over MCP except unused categories and empty projects.
  • Import. Clients can import a file or folder, optionally into a chosen bundle. AssetHoard asks you to allow or deny each import, showing the path, file count and size. No answer within a minute counts as deny. Turn on "Import without asking" in settings to skip the prompt.
  • Undo. Changes appear in the app immediately, with a toast, and go on the undo stack labelled "MCP:". A toolbar indicator shows when the server is running, and the settings page lists recent activity.

🔗 assethoard:// links

To help the MCP server link directly to assets, AssetHoard now registers assethoard:// file scheme. Please Note Linux distro's register the scheme, but some browsers might not respect it.

  • assethoard://asset/<id>, assethoard://bundle/<id> and assethoard://project/<id> links open AssetHoard at that item. If the app is already open it uses that window.
  • Assets, bundles and projects returned by the MCP server include a link, so your assistant can give you a clickable link.

🔊 Audio metadata

  • Search. AssetHoard reads embedded metadata from WAV (Broadcast Wave and RIFF info), MP3, FLAC and Ogg files: description, comment, keywords, title, artist, album, genre and year. All search modes match on it, so searching "shatter" finds SFX_0472_FINAL.wav if that's in its description.
  • Existing libraries are updated in the background. Except for packages/archives. Please reimport them to update the id3 tags
  • Details panel. A new File metadata section shows these fields.
  • Editing. Click the pencil next to File metadata to edit the tags. Changes are written back into MP3, WAV and FLAC files, so other tools see them too. Ogg is read-only for now.

  • Import options. When importing audio, you can turn keywords into tags, genre into a category and the embedded title into the asset name. The same actions are in the details panel for individual files.
  • Faster imports. Waveforms are now generated the first time you view a sound, not during import.

🌅 EXR and HDR

  • .exr and .hdr files now get thumbnails, previews, dimensions and image search. They also show in Associated Files and material previews.
  • EXR, HDR and float TIFF files can be exported as EXR, keeping full range and alpha. PNG, JPEG, GIF and TGA exports of these files are now colour-corrected instead of coming out dark.
  • When a file can't be previewed (unsupported EXR compression, deep images, too large to decode), the preview says why, and Export As is hidden.

To get thumbnails for EXR and HDR files already in your library, right-click and choose Reimport.

🖼️ Export As

  • Image… replaces the format list and the Resized… item. Pick format and size in one dialog. Size defaults to original, and there's a new Percentage option.
  • Batch export. Select several images and choose Export As > Image… to resize and convert them all into one folder. Images are only ever scaled down. Choose Nearest for pixel art or Smooth for everything else. The dialog shows each file's before and after size, and name clashes get (2) appended.
  • Crop… saves a region of an image as a new file at full resolution. Drag a box or type the coordinates, with optional aspect ratio presets.

🗂️ Organising

  • You can now create a category from any category dropdown, and from Set category and Manage Categories. Thanks to cpt_nightmare for the suggestion.
  • Category names must be unique (case-insensitive). Existing duplicates aren't changed. Use Merge in Settings to combine them.
  • Projects can be created, edited and deleted from the sidebar. Deleting asks first and can be undone. Projects now use the same colour picker as tags.
  • Bundles have a new Manage > Reimport All Assets option, which includes sub-bundles and shows how many assets will be reimported first.

📚 Large libraries

  • Fixed a disk-heavy check that could run for minutes after launch on libraries with lots of zips and Unity packages.
  • Orphan scans run in the background, and the cleanup list shows the first 200 missing files.
  • Fixed "too many SQL variables" errors when deleting large bundle trees, removing many orphans, or working with very large selections.
  • Undoing a delete of 40,000 assets now takes a couple of seconds instead of several minutes.

🐛 Fixes

  • Undoing Add to Project no longer removes the whole project. Undoing a project rename or description change now works.
  • Undoing a drag that moved assets and bundles together now refreshes the open bundle.
  • Exiting a search inside a bundle returns you to the bundle and clears the search box. Searches no longer run twice.
  • Zoomed image previews are sharper.
  • Deleting a category clears it from bundle category chips immediately.
  • Adding a tag with the same name as a deleted tag now restores the old tag instead of failing.

Happy hoarding.
Export any 3D model as a turntable GIF, sprite sheet or single frame. Unreal meshes and materials now preview with their textures, and models drag out of the library with their textures included.

AssetHoard is a local-first asset manager for game developers and digital artists. This release adds a turntable generator for 3D models, textured previews for Unreal meshes and materials, and exports that include a model's textures.

🎠 Turntable generator

Right-click a 3D model and choose Turntable to render it spinning. Export the result as an animated GIF, a sprite sheet, a zip of PNG frames or a single frame. Rendering happens on your own GPU.

  • Shot settings. Settings cover frame count, resolution, starting angle, camera height, padding, spin direction and frame rate. The background can be transparent or a solid colour, and you can add an outline in any colour and thickness.
  • Preview. The preview opens paused so you can frame the model first. You can then play it, slow it down or step through one frame at a time. The Spin/Sheet toggle in the top right shows the frames laid out as they'll appear in the sprite sheet.
  • Animation sheets. If a model has animation clips, set the frame source to Animation and pick a clip. The camera stays fixed and the clip plays across the frames. To build a directional character sheet, change the viewing angle and export once per direction. Clips where the character moves forward, like a walk or run, are kept centred in the frame.
  • No clipped frames. Animation sheets use a grid sized to the largest frame in the clip, with every frame lined up on the same pivot point. Long reaches and punches stay inside the cell, and the character is the same size as in a spin sheet.
  • Packaged models. Models inside a .unitypackage, .zip or other archive open with their textures, the same as loose files. If the original package has been moved, the generator tells you.

🎮 Unreal meshes and materials

  • Textured meshes. StaticMesh and SkeletalMesh previews now follow the mesh's materials and apply base colour, normal, roughness, metallic, ambient occlusion and emissive maps. Previously they rendered grey.
  • Material spheres. Unreal Materials and Material Instances now preview as a lit sphere you can rotate, with their textures applied, as Godot materials already did. Common Unreal suffixes such as _BC, _N and _ORM are recognised. UI, sprite and gradient materials still use their baked thumbnail.
  • Approximate previews. Both previews are marked "Approximate preview". AssetHoard treats the material as a standard PBR material, so the result is close to Unreal's but not identical.
  • Cooked packages. Cooked .uasset files have their editor data stripped out, so there's nothing to render. They now show a "Cooked Unreal package" notice that explains this.

🧊 3D model previews

  • OBJ textures. OBJ thumbnails in the library now use the diffuse texture from the model's .mtl file. For Blender exports where the .mtl only sets a colour, AssetHoard looks for textures in a nearby Textures/ folder.
  • FBX texture folders. FBX models with textures in a Textures/ subfolder now show them in the 3D preview as well as the thumbnail. The "Some textures couldn't load" warning no longer appears for these models.
  • FBX texture slots. FBX previews now read which texture goes in which slot from the file itself. The filename is only used as a fallback, and that matching is stricter, so a colour map named Bark_NormalTree.png is no longer treated as a normal map.
  • Material colours. The preview panel has a new Materials section listing each material's name and colour. This is mostly useful for models that use flat colours with no textures. Existing FBX files need a reimport to show it.

📤 Exporting and dragging out

  • Models with their textures. Dragging a 3D model out of the library, or right-clicking and choosing Export with textures, now copies its textures and materials alongside it. This works for FBX, OBJ, glTF and DAE. Missing textures are skipped and the export still completes.
  • Resized images. You can now export a resized copy of an image. The export keeps the image's proportions.
  • Bundles as folders. Dragging a bundle out creates a folder named after the bundle, with nested bundles as subfolders. Bundles stored on a network drive can be dragged out too.
  • Linux drag-out. Dragging assets out on Linux now works on both Wayland and X11, into Godot, your file manager or any other app. File names with non-English characters are kept intact, and a drag that fails no longer stops later drags from working.

🔍 Search and selection

  • Tag search. Type #tagname in the search box to show only assets with that tag, or #"multi word" for tags containing spaces. Tag search isn't case-sensitive and can be combined with normal search terms (dragon #fantasy) and with file type filters like *.png.
  • Deleting from search results. Deleted items are removed from the grid immediately. Undo brings them back.
  • Box selection. Dragging a selection box is now faster in very large libraries.

👀 Watched folders

  • Ignore patterns. You can now set ignore patterns for a watched folder, such as *.psd, *.blend1 or **/node_modules. Type a pattern and press space or enter, use quotes for patterns with spaces ("Saved Games/**"), or pick one from the quick-add list. Invalid patterns are rejected when you add them. Changes take effect without a restart.
  • Settings layout. Watched folder settings are grouped into three sections: Source, What gets imported and Applied to every import. Nothing is hidden in collapsed panels.
  • Sync status. The header shows the watch status and when the folder last synced, for example "Synced 4 minutes ago", with the full date on hover. Scan now has a text label, and Stop watching has moved to the footer, away from Save changes.
  • Fixes. "Last synced" no longer shows the wrong time in some time zones, and custom licence text from older setups is kept when you edit a watched folder.

🐛 Fixes

  • Reimports. Reimporting a folder now updates the previews of changed files. Previously the old version could show until you restarted the app.
  • Dragging from archives. Dragging an asset that lives inside an archive out of AssetHoard now drags just that asset, not the whole archive.
  • App menu. The gear icon in the sidebar now opens a menu with About Asset Hoard, What's New, Settings, Check for Updates and Quit. About opens in its own window.
  • Closing windows. Dragging inside a modal and releasing the mouse outside it no longer closes the window.

Happy hoarding.
